summary: Ethan Kroll worked in Indology and other fields. He held posts attested in 2012 at Baker McKenzie and as an editorial board member for Anthem South Asian Normative Traditions Studies.

Etienne Vermeersch (1934–2019) was a philosopher who studied at Ghent University from around 1953 to 1965. He later served on the faculty at Ghent University from 1967 to 1997, where he taught S. N. Balagangadhara.

Working in Indology and philosophy, Etsuaki Teraishi held posts at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College, attested in 1999, and as a special researcher at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science, attested in 2001.

Eugen Hultzsch (1857–1927) was an Indologist educated at Kreuzschule, Leipzig, and Vienna under Georg Bühler. He worked as an epigraphist for Madras and the Government of India, and held chairs at Vienna, Madras, and Halle-Wittenberg (1903–1925).

Eugen Pander (1854–1894) studied at Polytechnikum Riga and worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. In 1881, he was appointed professor of economics and lecturer in Russian and German at Tongwen Guan.
Eugen Prym (1843–1913) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at the University of Bonn from around 1861 to 1867 and subsequently held a post there from circa 1870 to 1913.

Eugen Wilhelm (1842–1923) specialized in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under August Schleicher from circa 1864 to 1868 and served as a professor at the University of Jena from around 1870 to 1917.

Eugene Watson Burlingame (1876–1932) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Charles Rockwell Lanman. He held appointments at the University of Pennsylvania (~1910–1914), Johns Hopkins University (~1914–1917), and Yale University (~1917–1932).

Eugene Y. Wang studied under Hung Wu and John M. Rosenfield. Working in art history, Buddhist studies, and Sinology, he held posts at the University of Chicago (~1996–1997) and Harvard University, serving as Abby Aldrich Rockefeller Professor of Asian Art.
Eugeni d'Ors (1881–1954) was a philosopher. He studied at the University of Barcelona from around 1897 to 1903 and at Universidad Central from around 1903 to 1905, where he later held a post.

Eugenius Marius Uhlenbeck (1913–2003) was a linguist who studied at Leiden University from circa 1932 to 1941. He later succeeded C. C. Berg as a professor at Leiden University, serving from 1950 to 1983.

Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz (1901–1981) was a Polish linguist and Indologist. After studying at the University of Lviv (~1919–1924), he held positions at Lviv (~1928–1939), Nicolaus Copernicus University (~1945–1953), and the University of Warsaw (~1953–1971).

Eugène Burnouf (1801–1852) was a French Indologist and scholar of Buddhism and Iranian studies who studied under Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He held posts at the Société Asiatique and succeeded Chézy at the Collège de France (1832–1852).
Eugène Jacquet (1811–1838) was an Indologist and linguist. He pursued his studies under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat from around 1828 to 1832, and later under Eugène Burnouf from around 1832 to 1838.

Eugène Obermiller (1901–1935) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy and Dondub Buddhayin, later serving as Section Secretary at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1930–1935).

Eugène Tisserant (1884–1972) worked in the fields of history, archaeology, and religious studies. He was educated at Lycée Notre-Dame Saint-Sigisbert, École du Louvre (~1905–1908), and Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1905–1908).

Eun Hino (born 1981) is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed a master's degree at the University of Tokyo (~2005–2007). Hino held posts at the University of Tokyo (~2011–2015) and Musashino University (~2015–2018).
Eun Maeda (1857–1930) was a Japanese scholar of Buddhist studies who taught Kozui Otani. He served as president of both Toyo University and Ryukoku University.

Eun-su Cho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed a PhD at UC Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini. Cho taught at the University of Michigan until 2004 and became professor at Seoul National University in 2004.
Eunyoung Choe (born 1968) is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at Korea University. Choe served as an HK Professor at Geumgang University, attested between 2013 and 2015.
